I have been looking for a shooter roguelike with coop compatibility to play with a friend, and this ain't it. I have pros and cons, but one outweigh the other. Pros : Pretty game, both for audio and visual beauty. The scenery is breathtaking, and the music is strange but it fits the gameplay. The spells and their interactions are wonderful. They look and feel good and I'd love to see what else they pair with. The enemies are imposing and their attacks feel strong, I'm glad after dodging one of their lasers or their wave attacks. Cons : I kept falling down the edges of maps, even right off the rip at the start of a level (Skill Issue, I know). But that's not the only issue I have with map generation. I kept getting stuck on the map, the details and crevices kept me from moving around. The combat is slow, I don't feel like my weapons hit hard at all and since most of the enemies are quite large, I can't seem to dodge adequately. The movement is quite floaty - as in it's realistic. No directional input while mid air. The game is empty, so empty. I get it, it's for the aesthetics of new, unexplored worlds and it's quite thrilling, but for gameplay, it's a hindrance. All in all, I enjoyed my time with the game, but after an hour of getting stuck on rocks in empty maps, I knew that replayability for this game wasn't for me. Worth a shot though if you like skill-based shooters with roguelike elements.

[h1]《The Black Pool》简评[/h1] 游戏类型 经典传统机制，肉鸽构筑体系，3D动作射击游戏。 游戏玩法 一个大区域内包含三个空间（房间），最后一个房间Boss战斗，每通过一个房间，随机抽取一项新的能力或者增幅。 构筑体系 行动方面——普通的快速攻击、普通的区域攻击、强攻、跳跃、冲刺、集结； 元素方面——火焰、闪电、大地、冰、风、光、辐射、虚空等； 每一次战斗，各项行动可以各自选择一个技能，选中后便不能再更换，之后再次选择便是对于元素属性的提升内容。游戏构筑体系，8大元素、88种能力与增幅升级、18种可升级的设备能力，包括了行动和元素之间元素属性、行动和行动之间操作组合、元素和元素之间的元素反应等。 地图世界 绯红之野世界、破碎陨石坑世界、熔岩之柱世界、黑曜石世界、冰岛世界、天空之地世界、幽暗世界、锯齿山峰世界、玛格努斯世界等。 能否联机 可以，最多支持四人联机，并且根据游戏以元素为核心的构筑体系以及元素反应机制，多人联机对战的战斗体验，应该是是胜过单人的。 剧情故事 超能力和科幻并存的世界观，类似于主神空间的“黑池”将玩家带到了一个未知的世界，玩家需要通过对超能力的选择和掌控，在各具特色的不同世界中穿梭旅行，击败一个接一个科幻感极强的敌人，最终找到回家的道路。 美术风格 科幻感十足，3D建模也还不错。 游戏不足 游戏目前还有不少缺陷，只能说很有潜力、有待挖掘更多内容。 （1）BUG问题：分辨率更换后无变化或者鼠标对准判定出错；游戏有闪退现象，闪退后不能续关接着来，只能重新开始打（商店页面提到的“恢复机制”，是没有触发的）。 （2）游戏构筑体系，可以选择的技能太少，选中后固定不变，无法中途根据随机内容进行变更，一局游戏的角色成长路线过于死板固定。 （3）游戏中提及有55种敌人（包括11种独特的多阶段BOSS遭遇战），但是实际上所面对的敌人感觉重复度特别高。 （4）游戏的引导薄弱，包括一开始刚进入到游戏，玩家从“黑池”中出来后，需要前往战斗世界，需要自己找路，路程还不短；以及各种战斗所需要的按键操作、行动说明等，也完全没有。 （5）光暗问题，部分地图的色调偏暗系，科技十足的敌人也是暗色皮肤，在这些地图中不是很能够看清楚环境和敌人。 （6）游戏射击手感不错，但是瞄准准星太小了，看不清，敌人高频率移动，很难找到准星瞄准。 综合评价 基础框架已经搭建完毕，但是细节不够完善；综合质量制作尚可，但是游戏部分瑕疵影响体验；构筑体系要素丰富，但是角色成长路线很固定死板；战斗射击手感和视觉特效不错，但是瞄准不太方便；美术风格科技感十足，但是部分场景实现暗淡难以看清。游戏潜力挺好、未来可期，但是需要打磨完善、不断优化。 [quote]关注[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url= https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]

[h1]Pretty good indie roguelite that deserve more attention.[/h1] [code]Pros: ✔️Fast paced and skill based combat. ✔️Satisfying movement systems. ✔️Tons of upgrades and skills for varied playstyles. ✔️Lot of different environments. ✔️Amazing graphics. ✔️Good procedural generation. ✔️Nice progression system. ✔️Can be played solo or co-op. ✔️Mysterious and intriguing atmosphere ✔️Fairly priced.[/code] [code]cons: ❌No FOV options. ❌Uninspired enemies design. (they don't look bad.) ❌Certain enemies have hitscan beams and they can feel cheap and poorly balanced. ❌Sometimes the physics are weird. ❌No skins or customization for characters. ❌Soundtrack is not very good. (subjective.) [/code] If you enjoyed games like Returnal and Risk of Rain 2 you should definitely give The Black Pool a try. Of course it's far from perfect because there's only two persons working on this but it's very enjoyable in it's current state and there's lot of room for improvements. The Black Pool is well worth the price of admission, it's highly replayable and fun to play. Hopefully this game gain more attention so they can keep updating and creating content for it. Keep it up developers, your game is good and have tons of potential. [h1]Rating 7.5/10.[/h1]

I'm a big fan of roguelikes, and FPS/3rd person shooter roguelikes are very fun. But for some reason this game just felt very bad to play. Controlling the character felt floating and clunky, the dodge roll was slow and hardly moves the player. The teleport jump upgrade felt great, possibly a different 'dash' power up would have made the game felt more smooth. Another big downfall of the game was even your light attacks have a cooldown. You spent a lot of the game just not attacking and waiting for everything, including what should be a spammable basic attack, come back. I ended up feeling like I was waiting for the enemy to die more than I was actively killing the enemy. The base speed of the character should really be increased to give you the feeling of high speed action dodging combat, but you just kind of spam double jump and use abilities on CD until the area is cleared and repeat until the end. I will say the final sequence area felt well done and nice, but the entire rest of the game felt like an unfinished college project. It just wasn't for me.

I really want to recommend this game. Everything about this game sounds really cool on paper. I love the worlds and the abilities but there is a lot holding this game back from being good and it really comes down to mostly some pretty egregious design choices. At the beginning of every game you get to choose from one of three elements and decide what you want to use them as: quick attack, area attack, charge attack, dash, jump, or rally. This sounds good but when you are first starting out you really have no idea what any of the elements provide to you and there is no tool tip until you select an element. This is the first issue. When you select an element, you are locked to that element no matter what. So if you just want to check out the skills, you can't. How would I know if I actually want to pick fire if I don't know how it'll change my gameplay? It's a shame that I can't preview abilities before I lock in. My second major criticism is how enemies spawn in. you will go through each lvl, and much like other games, enemies will spawn in at regular intervals. However, here the enemies can spawn behind you and regularly will. Sometimes they will spawn so close that there will be no time to react to it. This is terrible considering a lot of the enemies will either blow up in your face or have crazy strong aoe attacks. And the fact that some enemies have large health bars compounds the issue even further. if it was just grunt enemies then maybe I could let it slide but sometimes even elite enemies can spawn behind you. The third thing would be that the tracking on some enemy abilities is waaaay higher than it should be. In particular for me, there is a 4 legged tank enemy that regulary shoots out homing pulse blasts and even with a good dodge there is a good chance the attack can still curve to hit you anyway. This was a lesser complaint. And finally, the big thing that locks this game down for me is overall visibility of enemies and maps (I'm looking at you Gloom map). Will so many reflective surfaces in the game, and there are a lot, some enemies are either really small or blend in with the environment since most of them are robotic and reflective in their own right. This makes seeing enemies incredibly hard on certain maps. And then there is a map that is so dark that enemies are incredibly hard to see which is even worse when you realize that they can always see you and if you dare stand in one of the spotlights by either dodging or moving out of attacks, you can basically blind your vision that's already disadvantaged. I want to like this game and again I hope the devs continue to work on something because there is a lot of promise here but some fundamental changes need to happen before I can recommend this as is. I'm hoping I can change this review int he future.

I'm not even a fan of shmups but the weird otherworldly nature of this game with its rogue-like elements mixed in is a fever dream. I'm shocked it hasn't gotten more ink or reviews. It might be the time it released... that was right around a certain massive DLC everyone was waiting for. Whatever the reason may be, this gem shouldn't be overlooked. You play as one of 4 ugly kids. You drop into this grim main chamber and pick your starting powers that are randomized. It's a godsend when you get a rare or better off the rip. Then, you make your way into the meat of it and worlds vary. They are all kinds of strange. They are almost liminal spaces that feel familiar yet aren't. I'm talking rocky planets, floating islands, strange suburban 'hoods, and more. It's also co-op which is wonderful and adds to the madness onscreen. Make no mistake, this is more of a shmup and the chaos on screen is nuts! I love it. It's colorful, trippy and hypnotic. It also has a FEEL. You know? When you want to play a game and its very theme permeates into you. That's what this game does. It's also quite good looking and decently optimized. Though, if you look at my profile, I can throw my rig at an unoptimized game so... who knows. It's an easy recommendation. This small studio made a wonderful game here. I'd like to see what else they are up to. I'd be interested in them exploring the weird suburban theme deeper.

I wanted so badly to love this game. An action roguelike with wacky abilities, unique enemies, and a slightly weird setting - it's everything that I want in a game. Unfortunately it's marred by extremely bad balancing and poor design choices. Many abilities are just terrible or completely impractical to use, a few regular enemies are harder than the level bosses (i.e. colossus), certain maps make it hard to see or easy to get stuck, and so on. I'm really sad to give this a thumbs down, but most runs ended up being infuriating in unfun ways. ----- [i]Edit to detail my issues with various abilities.[/i] There are some fun abilities in the game. And others that I can appreciate as creative or interesting. The problem is too many skills are dull or ineffective, leading me to finish most runs unsatisfied. [b]Area attacks:[/b] Enemies move around so much and stay so spread out, if you're lucky you hit one target who leaves the area immediately. Most Area attacks are very short range or body-centered but don't do enough damage to make up for the risk of getting so close to enemies especially considering the lack of healing. Most don't work at all against flying or distant enemies, including several bosses. Super long cooldowns compound these problems. Generally I pray to get good Quick and Strong attacks because Area attacks are so useless. - Light's diameter is particularly small, plus you can't use other attacks while charging it, making it extremely difficult and risky to use. - Fire is the most annoying, its overwhelming visual effect makes it impossible to see anything. - Ice's small area and lack of DoT means you have to pray whatever you hit stands in it for it to do any damage at all. - Wind covers a nice area and its projectile actually travels, unfortunately it's so weak (even when upgraded) it's more of a utility skill for picking off scattered low-health enemies. - Terra's turrets are nice, but again their damage is so low even when heavily upgraded that they only help against the weakest of foes. [b]Quick attacks:[/b] Most are just little round projectiles that go in a single direction. They don't hit hard, it's difficult to hit enemies due to the slow projectiies, they're boring/repetitive to use, and they quickly go on cooldown. - Decay, Fire, Chaos, Ice, Terra, and Void fall into this category. - Terra is the worst, the summoning animation adds an extra click and short delay before shooting, which means in a firefight I can never be sure if my shot is going to just go or if it will just start an animation and mess with my aim and timing. - Void is by far the most effective since its homing effect means it usually hits something. It can easily be the highest damaging skill in a run but it is incredibly boring to use. [b]Strong attacks:[/b] Generally the most fun and powerful. But long cooldowns means they get limited use. - Terra's pillar is just not practical in a fight. Positioning yourself behind a stationary object to line up a shot is basically suicide. Add to that the way you have to be right next to it to hit anything above ground level, and this is probably the worst attack in the game. - Chaos boomerang is incredibly difficult to catch even when not in a fight, meaning it's really just an okay projectile attack with no upside. - Ice I had a hard time blocking attacks, with so many coming from random sides, so mostly it just felt like a projectile attack, like Chaos. [b]Dashes + Jumps:[/b] Some are better than others (especially stuff that lets you avoid damage, i.e. Fire flight, Decay invuln, Lightning teleport), but almost all are generally fun or useful. [b]Rally:[/b] Really hard to use due to boss fights requiring lots of moving around. Generally when I used a Rally, it didn't impact the fight at all because it got left behind almost immediately. As a result I can't really comment on these. Kind of a bummer. I really enjoyed a few of the abilities (Wind quick attack, Void/Light/Air strong attack) and there were others that I didn't love but were fine to use. The problem is I felt like there were too many bad ones with no way to avoid them.

The Black Pool, developed and published by Smug Marmot Studios, is a kinetic and cooperative-focused action roguelike that builds its identity around speed, synergy, and the unpredictability of each run. It places players in a strange, otherworldly setting tied together by the mysterious titular pool, using that premise as a springboard for a loop centered on repeated attempts, gradual mastery, and evolving character builds. While the setup is familiar within the genre, the execution leans heavily into momentum and teamwork, giving the experience a distinct rhythm that separates it from more methodical roguelikes. Combat is the backbone of the game, and it is designed to be fast, reactive, and constantly demanding. Encounters unfold in rapid bursts, requiring players to stay mobile, read enemy patterns quickly, and make split-second decisions. There is little room for hesitation, as the game rewards aggressive play balanced with awareness of positioning and timing. This creates a sense of flow that can feel exhilarating once mastered, with each successful encounter reinforcing the player’s ability to maintain control amid chaos. The emphasis on movement and responsiveness gives the gameplay a sharp, energetic feel that keeps each run engaging. A key element that drives replayability is the game’s flexible ability system. Throughout each run, players acquire and upgrade powers that can be combined in a variety of ways, leading to builds that can differ dramatically from one session to the next. Rather than pushing players toward a single optimal strategy, the game encourages adaptation, asking players to work with what they are given and discover effective combinations on the fly. This constant variation adds depth to the experience, as understanding how abilities interact becomes just as important as mechanical skill. Over time, players develop a stronger sense of how to shape their builds, turning early uncertainty into deliberate experimentation. The cooperative aspect is where The Black Pool truly finds its strongest identity. Designed with multiplayer at its core, the game supports groups working together through each run, and many of its systems are built to reward coordination. Abilities can interact in ways that amplify their effectiveness when used in tandem, creating opportunities for teamwork that feel both intentional and impactful. This focus on synergy transforms the gameplay from an individual challenge into a shared experience, where communication and collaboration become central to success. While the game remains playable solo, it is clear that its full potential is realized when played with others. Progression follows a familiar roguelite structure, blending temporary, run-based upgrades with longer-term unlocks that persist between attempts. Each run contributes to a broader sense of growth, gradually expanding the player’s capabilities and options. This system helps maintain motivation even in failure, as progress is rarely lost entirely. At the same time, the balance between randomness and persistence ensures that no two runs feel exactly the same, preserving the sense of unpredictability that defines the genre. Visually, the game presents a vibrant and stylized world that supports its fast-paced design. The environments are varied and visually distinct, offering a sense of progression as players move through different areas. Effects are clear and readable, an essential quality given the intensity of combat, allowing players to track enemies and abilities without becoming overwhelmed. The presentation works in service of the gameplay, enhancing clarity and immersion without distracting from the action. However, the game does face some challenges that are common within the roguelike genre. The procedural structure, while providing variety, can also lead to moments of repetition, particularly during extended play sessions. Additionally, the lack of a robust onboarding experience may make the early stages feel somewhat opaque, as players are left to piece together systems and mechanics through trial and error. For solo players, the difficulty curve can feel steeper, as the game’s systems are clearly tuned with cooperative play in mind. Despite these limitations, The Black Pool succeeds in delivering a focused and engaging experience that thrives on its strengths. It captures the excitement of fast-paced combat while layering in meaningful build variety and cooperative interaction, creating a gameplay loop that feels both dynamic and rewarding. Its design encourages players to improve not just individually but as part of a team, reinforcing the importance of coordination and adaptability. In the end, The Black Pool stands out as a confident and energetic entry in the action roguelike space, offering a compelling mix of speed, strategy, and collaboration. While it may not completely avoid the repetition inherent to the genre, it provides enough depth and variety to keep players invested, particularly when shared with others. Rating: 8/10

Love this genre, but The Black Pool just doesn't do it for me. Some skills feel critically important; some are near useless. Every enemy is a generic sci-fi construct that shoot generic 'beams' or 'balls'. The game feels like it's lacking a lot of sound effects, so the combat feels oddly quiet and insignificant. The temporary power-ups are as temporary as they can be; I never feel like I'm getting stronger in any way. I kept trying to enjoy it but it just never became fun. Oh, and though this doesn't affect gameplay, the character models you can pick look deeply unsettling. Like 40-somethings with a child's body. It'd have been better to just have faceless, generic astronauts or something considering the rest of the aesthetics in the game.

I want to like this game but it's ROUGH. The premise is cool: think of Returnal but low budget. Cool skill combo ideas, some very original skill mechanics... But also some really underwhelming ones. Sound design is all over the place: the music is cool but the sound effects are mostly awful. Skills with cool visual effects lack punch in their audio, making them feel wimpy. Aside from that, as mentioned at the start the game is really rough. Movement is floaty and imprecise, camera does weird things often and the controls are not very responsive. All three are very important features for a roguelike. All in all, the game has good bones but I don't think the developer plans on growing it much further. I'd only advice getting this if you're starved for a new 3D action roguelite and wanna try something different. But be prepared for the jank, and get it at a sale.
